title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
event_hint: CodeNib: a multi-view repository-context data system that materializes reusable lexical (BM25/Zoekt), dense (FAISS), and structural (graph) views per commit, incrementally maintains selected-view deltas across edits, and serves ranked search, symbol navigation, and bounded context through one runtime (with stdio MCP + LSP-shaped skill adapters) to coding agents.
problem: Coding agents repeatedly search, navigate, and retain context from evolving repositories, but today's indexes, language servers, and task-local histories are disconnected: they force repeated discovery, do not map outputs back to a common commit and repository-relative source range, and obscure lifecycle costs (per-edit rebuild vs incremental maintenance). Three coupled challenges: C1 heterogeneous views (lexical/dense/structural need different physical layouts but must map to the same commit and source ranges); C2 incremental freshness (an edit changes each view differently, so graph repair, embedding reuse, and rebuild paths must be selected and evaluated separately); C3 agent delivery (serving bounded context through agent tools).
mechanism: CodeNib builds three reusable views per repository commit: lexical (BM25, optional Zoekt), dense (file-level L0 and callable-level L2 embeddings in FAISS), and structural (a reference graph used for dependency/definition/reference/route navigation). Outputs are mapped to repository-relative path/start-line ranges. Selected views are maintained across edits via incremental delta maintenance (graph repair, embedding reuse, rebuild paths chosen per view). One runtime serves search_semantic/search_bm25/search_regex/search_zoekt, structural tools (dependency subgraphs, definitions, references, routes), and get_manifest; missing optional indexes return explicit tool errors rather than silent fallback. Adapters: stdio MCP (instantiates static serving; exposes semantic/BM25/regex/Zoekt search + structural tools) and LSP-shaped skills (accept an injected static or live JSON-RPC provider, sharing the agent-facing location schema while traces record which backend served). AgentRunner separates index-backed SkillRegistry capabilities from ordinary ToolRegistry primitives; AgentRunTrace records ordered events/context state and UsageTracker records provider tokens. Two context policies are studied: Eager (keeps its prefix throughout) and Compact (deterministically resets the prefix once, after the complete tool batch containing the first successful read, restoring the clean issue + deduped paths + newest successful read + a 600-char direction cue copied from the latest nonempty assistant message; this transition is the policy's single cache discontinuity).

evidence.claim: Agent context-policy token/localization results (Q5, Figure 11a-b), five models (Claude Haiku 4.5, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-27B, Gemma 4-12B, Gemini 2.5 Flash), ordinary tools, 16-turn cap, frozen top-10 candidates, paired grep/read baseline (baseline volume 25.9-159.7K tokens/query). The selected context policy (Eager for Haiku, Compact otherwise) uses 49.9, 45.1, 44.8, 12.9, and 35.8% of paired grep/read tokens respectively (i.e. 50.1-87.1% fewer trajectory tokens). delta-AnswerRecall@5 ranges from -0.009 to +0.067, with all lower bounds above -0.05 (the no-change margin), so localization is preserved versus paired grep/read.
evidence.value: selected policy uses 12.9-49.9% of grep/read tokens (50.1-87.1% fewer); delta-AR@5 -0.009 to +0.067, all >= -0.05
evidence.condition: five models, 16-turn cap, frozen top-10 candidates, Eager/Compact selection rule, full provider-reported trajectories, zero recall for invalid answers

evidence.claim: Compaction is not uniformly dominant (Q5): Compact/Eager token usage ranges from 123.3% (Haiku) to 27.9% (Gemma) of paired grep/read; Gemma and Gemini trade 0.070 and 0.044 AnswerRecall@5 against Eager while still clearing the baseline gate. Workload effects (panel c, descriptive only, several quality intervals cross the margin, so no subgroup-routing claim) span query types (Behavioral 175, File hint 76, Module hint 75, Reasoning 50, Symbol hint 50, Traversal 74) and five languages (C/C++, Go, Python, Rust, TS/JS, 100 each).
evidence.value: Compact/Eager token 27.9-123.3% of grep/read; Gemma/Gemini trade 0.070/0.044 AR@5 vs Eager; no subgroup-routing claim
evidence.condition: five models, descriptive pooled workload/language slices

evidence.claim: Static vs live symbol-navigation latency (Q3, Figure 9): across 1,000 requests over 100 snapshots, 632 (63.2%) normalized path/start-line sets match the live JSON-RPC provider (437/500 definitions = 87.4%; 195/500 references = 39.0%). On the matching subset, static/live p50 = 0.62/2.26 ms, a median paired saving of 1.69 ms and a median live/static ratio of 4.72x. Match rate is the limiting result: definitions 80-99% across languages, references 22-73%.
evidence.value: 63.2% overall match; static p50 0.62 ms vs live 2.26 ms; median live/static 4.72x; def match 87.4%, ref match 39.0%
evidence.baseline: live JSON-RPC language servers (clangd, gopls, basedpyright, rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server)
evidence.condition: 100 snapshots, 1,000 requests (500 def + 500 ref), normalized path/start-line equality on matching subset only

evidence.claim: Incremental update speedup (Section 11 / Appendix F): on transitions matching an independent rebuild, graph-repair and vector-reuse reach 8.67x and 25.44x median speedups respectively (Section 11 conclusion); an independent Rust/TS rebuild cross-check reaches 99.75% median edge F1 and 99.35% serving agreement, and all 31 vector targets match artifact identities and vectors. Appendix G: each materialization uses an isolated quiescent checkout and fresh processes (warm-host, not cold-start; host caches not flushed, remote model weights not reloaded); the evaluated vector builder materializes both L0 and L2 even though the trace queries only L2, so lifecycle cost includes both.
evidence.value: graph-repair 8.67x median; vector-reuse 25.44x median; rebuild F1 99.75%, serving agreement 99.35%; 31/31 vector targets exact
evidence.condition: transitions matching independent rebuild; warm-host materialization, isolated checkout/fresh processes
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 15 (Section 11 Conclusion); PDF Page 22 (Appendix F, Appendix G Lifecycle Execution Boundary)

evidence.claim: Lifecycle session-cost projection (Appendix G Panel c): at q=20 controlled-trace scale, process-isolated and shared-resident projections are 13.20 s/session (95% CI 10.43-15.96) and 6.24 s/session (3.66-8.11); at q=100, medians are 8.53 and 1.27 s/session. Runtime view loading floors the process-isolated model; the shared-resident model approaches measured serve-only S/N, not a hardware floor. Only q=20 is the controlled trace scale; other q values project the same measured terms.
evidence.baseline: process-isolated vs shared-resident runtime view loading
evidence.condition: lifecycle trace S over N=20 sessions, warm-host, one warmup + three measured repetitions
evidence.source_locator: PDF Page 22 (Appendix G Lifecycle Execution Boundary, Panel c)

evaluation_context: 100 repository snapshots (C/C++, Go, Python, Rust, TS/JS). Views: lexical (BM25, optional Zoekt), dense (FAISS IndexFlatIP/IVFFlat/HNSWFlat; L0 file-level and L2 callable-level; five embedders SR-Small 137M, Qwen3-Embed-0.6B, Jina-Code-1.5B, Qwen3-Embed-4B, SR-Large 7B), structural (reference graph). Live comparators: clangd, gopls, basedpyright, rust-analyzer, typescript-language-server. Agent runs: five models (Claude Haiku 4.5, Qwen3.5-9B via vLLM 0.23.0 65K cap, Qwen3.5-27B via vLLM 0.23.0 65K cap, Gemma 4-12B via vLLM 0.25.1 131K cap, Gemini 2.5 Flash via Vertex AI thinkingBudget=0); ordinary tools, 16-turn cap, frozen top-10 candidates, 48K-token history, 4096-token completion, prefix caching; two context policies Eager (keeps prefix) and Compact (resets prefix once). Token axes sum provider-reported prompt/completion tokens (not cache-adjusted); zero recall for invalid answers. Retrieval/index params frozen per Table 7 (graph weight 0.5, RRF constant 60, HNSW M=32 ef_construction=200, IVF probes swept). Lifecycle: isolated quiescent checkout, fresh processes, warm-host (caches not flushed, weights not reloaded); the evaluated vector builder materializes both L0 and L2 even though only L2 is queried.
limitations: The supplement confirms the Q5 agent-loop token reduction: the selected context policy uses 12.9-49.9% of paired grep/read tokens (50.1-87.1% fewer) across the five named models with delta-AnswerRecall@5 all >= -0.05, so the abstract's '50-87% fewer trajectory tokens with localization preserved' is now verified (not just a claim). However: (1) compaction is not uniformly dominant (Compact/Eager token usage ranges 27.9-123.3% of grep/read; Haiku is worse than grep/read at 123.3%) and Gemma/Gemini trade 0.070/0.044 AR@5 against Eager; (2) token axes are provider-reported prompt/completion sums, NOT cache-adjusted cost, and cache hits/prefill latency are unmeasured, so the token reduction may not translate linearly to $/latency; (3) the Compact transition is the policy's single cache discontinuity and the authors do not claim the pre-transition cache survives it; (4) workload-effect slices (panel c) are descriptive with intervals crossing the margin, so no subgroup-routing claim is made; (5) the static-vs-live 4.72x latency ratio applies only to the 63.2% matching subset (references match as little as 22-33%); (6) ANN speedups remain component-local; (7) lifecycle model fits are descriptive; (8) concurrent publication, learned online scheduling, and post-training gains are explicitly out of scope (next system boundary); authentication/multi-tenancy/network transport and MCP as an experimental factor remain outside the evaluated stdio implementation.
project_relevance: Directly on-topic for the agent-acceleration card's question of reducing repeated Read/Grep/Glob and of whether a code knowledge graph / repository index lowers end-to-end task cost: CodeNib is a concrete multi-view (lexical+dense+structural) repository-context serving system exposing search/navigation/context through MCP tools and LSP-shaped skills. The now-verified Q5 result (selected context policy uses 12.9-49.9% of paired grep/read tokens with localization preserved across five models) is the most project-actionable number: it quantifies the trajectory-token reduction a structured repository-context service delivers versus naive grep/read, directly addressing the card's 'reduce repeated Read/Grep' goal, with the explicit caveat that compaction is model-dependent (Haiku is worse than grep/read) and tokens are not cache-adjusted cost. The 8.67x/25.44x incremental graph/vector update speedups and the 4.72x static-vs-live navigation latency (on matching subset) give concrete lifecycle and per-operation cost numbers.
